articles.title: Denver Broncos vs Pittsburgh Steelers Week 12: Streak Washed Out, 5-27
articles.matchup: Final: Pittsburgh Steelers (7-4) 27, Denver Broncos (8-3) 5, Fri., Nov. 27, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh. Next: vs Miami Dolphins, Sun., Dec. 6, 4:05 PM ET, Empower Field at Mile High, Denver
articles.text:
The Denver Broncos lost 27-5 to the Pittsburgh Steelers on a soggy afternoon in western Pennsylvania, and the six-game winning streak ends in the worst way. Kansas City had lost on Thanksgiving night. Sole possession of first place in the AFC West was sitting right there. We left it in the rain.

It went sideways early. On our second possession, the ball slipped out of Bo Nix's hand with the rush closing in, bounced into the end zone, and T.J. Watt fell on it. Then Mason Rudolph hit a 58-yard catch-and-run and a 22-yard touchdown, and we were down 14-0 in the first quarter.

We had a pulse in the second quarter. Alex Singleton tackled Jaylen Warren in the Pittsburgh end zone for a safety, and Wil Lutz hit a 44-yard field goal to make it 14-5. Then Pittsburgh kicked a field goal, and on our next snap Jalen Ramsey stepped in front of a throw meant for Jaylen Waddle and ran it back 36 yards. Two defensive touchdowns allowed in one half. That's the game.

Nix finished 22 of 40 for 169 yards, no touchdowns, two interceptions and three sacks. We managed 205 yards and 3.0 yards a play, went 4 of 15 on third down, and came away empty on our only red zone trip.

Singleton was the bright spot, 13 tackles and the safety. Jaylen Waddle caught five balls for 53 yards. Jonah Coleman caught eight. Tyler Badie gave us decent field position on kickoffs, 94 yards on four returns.

We held the ball for 33:52 and still lost by 22. That's three turnovers doing the damage, and two of them went for six.

We're 8-3, still very much in the AFC West race, and the Miami Dolphins visit Empower Field at Mile High on Sunday, Dec. 6, at 4:05 PM ET. Dry off, flush it, go win at home. Broncos Country, let's ride.

articles.title: Pittsburgh Steelers vs Denver Broncos Week 12: Defense Scores Twice, 27-5
articles.matchup: Final: Pittsburgh Steelers (7-4) 27, Denver Broncos (8-3) 5, Fri., Nov. 27, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh. Next: vs Houston Texans, Sun., Dec. 6, 8:20 PM ET, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh
articles.text:
After the week this franchise just lived through, I'd have taken a one-point win in the mud. Instead, the Pittsburgh Steelers buried the Denver Broncos 27-5 in the rain at Acrisure Stadium on Black Friday, and the defense outscored Denver by itself.

You know the backdrop. Aaron Rodgers is gone after a very public split, and the whole country spent the week laughing at us. So T.J. Watt and Cameron Heyward told this team to stay present, and the defense answered on Denver's second possession. Bo Nix had the ball slip out of his hand with Watt and Nick Herbig bearing down, and Watt fell on it in the end zone. 7-0. Mist and noise everywhere.

Mason Rudolph took it from there. He hit rookie Germie Bernard on a 58-yard catch-and-run, then lofted a 22-yard touchdown to DK Metcalf for a 14-0 lead, our first 14-0 first-quarter lead since 2019. Rudolph finished 9 of 15 for 142 yards, no interceptions, no drama. Exactly what we needed.

Denver got a safety when Alex Singleton dropped Jaylen Warren in our end zone, and a Wil Lutz field goal made it 14-5. Then Chris Boswell hit from 47, and on Denver's next snap Jalen Ramsey jumped a Nix throw and took it 36 yards to the house. 24-5 at halftime. Boswell added a 33-yarder in the fourth, and nobody in black and gold broke a sweat.

Nix was held to 169 yards on 40 throws, with two interceptions and three sacks. Daylen Everette grabbed the other interception. Payton Wilson made eight tackles. Denver managed 205 yards, and its six-game winning streak is done. Rico Dowdle ran for 71 yards on 11 carries.

We're 7-4, and the Houston Texans come to Acrisure Stadium for a Sunday night game on Dec. 6 at 8:20 PM ET. Turn the page. Here we go, Steelers.

articles.title: Minnesota vs Wisconsin: The Axe Goes Back to Madison, 5-28
articles.byline: Torvald 'Tor' Engebretsen, The Minnesota Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Wisconsin Badgers (8-4) 28, Minnesota Golden Gophers (6-6) 5, Fri., Nov. 27, Camp Randall Stadium, Madison. Regular season complete
articles.text:
Minnesota lost 28-5 at Wisconsin on Friday night, and Paul Bunyan's Axe goes back to Madison. I'm writing this from a very quiet corner of the Twin Cities.

It began with promise. On the Badgers' opening drive, Naiim Parrish jumped a Colton Joseph throw and returned it 18 yards, and Luke Drzewiecki banged home a 53-yard field goal. Minnesota 3, Wisconsin 0, and for about 10 minutes of game time I believed.

From there, Wisconsin scored touchdowns on three straight drives while we went three-and-out three straight times. At halftime it was 21-3, and the Badgers had 16 first downs to our one. One.

The final numbers are brutal. We were outgained 482-115 and outrushed 265-11. We had six first downs all night. Drake Lindsey completed 14 of 28 throws for 104 yards behind a front that couldn't hold up. Joseph ran for 101 yards and had a hand in three touchdowns against us. Our only other points came on a safety when Wisconsin was flagged for holding in its own end zone.

A few Gophers deserve a salute. Joey Gerlach made 12 tackles. Maverick Baranowski made seven and grabbed an interception. Parrish made the play that gave us the early lead. We didn't lose a fumble or throw an interception, and still couldn't keep pace. When you run for 11 yards on 14 carries, the defense ends up on the field for 38:54, and no defense in this league survives that.

The series is now tied at 64-64-8, and Wisconsin has beaten us just twice in six years. That's a stat I'll cling to until next November.

We're 6-6, 4-5 in the Big Ten, bowl eligible, and waiting on a destination. One more game to send this group out the right way, and a full offseason to figure out how to block Wisconsin. Ski-U-Mah.

articles.title: Wisconsin vs Minnesota: The Axe Comes Home to Madison, 28-5
articles.byline: Lars 'Brat' Ellefson, The Wisconsin Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Wisconsin Badgers (8-4) 28, Minnesota Golden Gophers (6-6) 5, Fri., Nov. 27, Camp Randall Stadium, Madison. Regular season complete
articles.text:
Paul Bunyan's Axe is back in Madison where it belongs. Wisconsin flattened Minnesota 28-5 on Black Friday night in front of 72,651 at Camp Randall, and the most-played rivalry in the FBS is now dead even at 64-64-8.

Colton Joseph was a one-man wrecking crew. He completed 12 of 18 throws for 217 yards, ran for 101 more on 20 carries, and scored three touchdowns. On third-and-13 on the first play of the second quarter, he found Tyrell Henry for a 27-yard score to put us ahead for good. He ran one in from 7 yards before the half, and from the 1 late in the third. Along the way he set the single-season rushing record for a Wisconsin quarterback, now at 659 yards.

The numbers look like a typo. We outgained the Gophers 482-115. We outrushed them 265-11. At halftime it was 21-3, and we had 16 first downs to their one. Bryan Jackson II added a 1-yard touchdown, and Darrion Dupree carried 23 times for 80 yards.

Minnesota got its points from a 53-yard field goal after an interception on our opening drive, and a holding flag in our end zone for a safety. The Gophers finished with six first downs. Cooper Catalano made seven tackles, and Tyreese Fearbry got a sack.

This defense has been a fortress at home all season. We allowed 44 points in six games at Camp Randall and never gave up more than 10 in any of them. AP says the last time a Wisconsin team did that was 1951.

We're 8-4, 6-3 in the Big Ten, and we doubled last season's number of wins. Joseph threw two interceptions, one off a receiver's hands, and we'll fix that before the bowl. Tonight, though, the Axe is ours, and it looks perfect in red. Somebody grab a saw. On, Wisconsin.

articles.title: Texas A&M vs Texas: Aggies Defend Kyle Field, Offense Can't Finish, 6-16
articles.byline: Colt Wendeborn, The Texas A&M Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Texas Longhorns (10-2) 16, Texas A&M Aggies (4-8) 6, Fri., Nov. 27, Kyle Field, College Station. Regular season complete
articles.text:
Texas A&M lost 16-6 to Texas at Kyle Field on Black Friday night, and the 109,570 of us who stood the whole way deserved a touchdown. One. Just one. The Aggies didn't find the end zone all night, and the season ends at 4-8.

Here's what kills me: our defense played well enough to win. Texas managed 242 yards and 2.9 yards a carry. Tawfiq Byard was a monster with 11 tackles and an interception in the end zone when Texas had a chance to put us away in the fourth quarter. Ray Coney made 11 tackles, too. The Longhorns needed three field goals to get to 16.

Brady Hart, in his second game as the No. 1 quarterback, threw for 201 yards on 22 of 35 with no interceptions. Aaron Gregory was outstanding, seven catches for 120 yards, including a 30-yarder in the third quarter that put us in scoring position. David Olano was money, hitting from 52 as time expired in the first half and from 35 to make it 13-6 in the third.

And then we stalled, drive after drive. The ground game finished with 33 yards on 25 carries. Mario Craver fumbled after a catch on our second snap of the second half, and Texas turned it into points. After Byard's interception, we failed on fourth down and handed it right back.

That's five straight losses to close the year, and a fourth straight loss to Texas. A season after we made the College Football Playoff for the first time, 4-8, 1-8 in the SEC, is hard to stomach.

But I'll tell you this: the 12th Man stood for every snap, and our defense gave this offense every chance. Fix the offense, and the rest is already here. Byard, Coney and that defense showed the bones are there, and I'll be back in my seat next fall. Gig 'em.

articles.title: Texas vs Texas A&M: Spetic's Boot Punches the Ticket to Atlanta, 16-6
articles.byline: Caro Whitfield, The Texas Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Texas Longhorns (10-2) 16, Texas A&M Aggies (4-8) 6, Fri., Nov. 27, Kyle Field, College Station. Regular season complete
articles.text:
It wasn't art. It was a 16-6 grind in front of 109,570 in College Station the night after Thanksgiving, and Texas walked out of Aggieland with a fourth straight win against the Aggies and a ticket to the SEC Championship Game. I'll take ugly in that building every single year.

Gianni Spetic was the MVP of my heart. He opened the scoring with a 54-yard field goal in the first quarter, hit from 33 in the third, and drilled a 42-yarder with 5:19 left to make it a two-score game. Three kicks, three makes, 10 points.

Arch Manning had a tough night, 18 of 34 for 143 yards, but he engineered the drive that mattered most: 12 plays, 88 yards, capped by a 3-yard touchdown to Cam Coleman early in the second quarter for a 10-0 lead. Yes, a tipped throw got intercepted in the end zone in the fourth. The defense shrugged and got the ball right back on a fourth-down stop.

That defense was the story. The Aggies ran 25 times for 33 yards. Rasheem Biles made nine tackles, and Justin Cryer and Brad Spence each recorded a sack. Jelani McDonald recovered a fumble on the Aggies' second snap of the second half, and we turned it into Spetic's 33-yarder after converting a fourth-and-1. Texas A&M never scored a touchdown.

Michael Terry III ran for 50 yards on 12 carries. Ryan Wingo caught five balls. It wasn't flashy. It didn't need to be. Championship teams find a way on nights when the offense sputters, and this one found it in a hostile building on the last Friday of November.

Texas sits at 10-2, 7-2 in the SEC, winners of six straight, and now it's top-ranked Georgia in Atlanta on Dec. 5. Last time we met the Bulldogs for the conference crown, we lost 22-19 in overtime. I haven't forgotten. Neither has this team. Hook 'em.

articles.title: Air Force vs New Mexico: Falcons Fade in Albuquerque, 19-42
articles.byline: Lt. Col. (Ret.) Marissa Okonkwo-Hale, The Air Force Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: New Mexico Lobos (10-2) 42, Air Force Falcons (9-3) 19, Fri., Nov. 27, University Stadium (NM), Albuquerque. Regular season complete
articles.text:
Air Force lost 42-19 at New Mexico on the last Friday of November, and the score doesn't tell you how close this was midway through the third quarter. We were down two points with the ball rolling our way. Then the Lobos found another gear, and we didn't.

It began like a dream. Evan Medders ran in from the 1 on our opening drive, 7-0. Then came the 52-yard Lobo touchdown run, and on our very next snap, we fumbled at our own 24. Two plays later, it was 14-7. That 54-second stretch hurt, and it took the air out of a fast opening.

We kept fighting. Carter Cremascoli hit two 25-yard field goals, the second one with two seconds left in the half. Medders scored again from 6 yards out in the third quarter, and it was 21-19. We went for two to tie it. The try ended in a fumble, and the moment slipped away.

From there New Mexico scored three straight touchdowns. Luke Moga threw for 248 yards and three scores, and Kiefer Sibley ran for 115.

Medders gave us all he had: 11 of 22 for 193 yards, 57 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 22 carries. Adam Hrynciw caught three balls for 68 yards, and Mason Hayes had a 43-yarder. Max Mustell intercepted Moga and made eight tackles, and Brody Bujnoch made nine. We went 3 for 5 on fourth down and held the ball for 32:13. That's Falcon football.

But we gave up 182 rushing yards on just 29 carries, and New Mexico hit too many big plays for us to keep pace.

We're 9-3, 5-3 in the Mountain West, and we expect a bowl invitation soon. Nine wins from a team of future officers is worth a salute, and one more game in December sounds right. Fly, Fight, Win.

Only the second 10-win season in program history. The most conference wins we've ever had. Our first trip to the Mountain West title game. I've waited my whole life to type those sentences.

Kiefer Sibley set the tone. Down 7-0, he broke a 52-yard touchdown run with 3:20 left in the first quarter. On Air Force's very next snap, Mercury Swaim punched the ball loose, Brett Karhu recovered at the Falcons' 24, and two plays later Ricklan Holmes II plowed in from the 1. Fourteen points in less than a minute, and we never trailed again. Sibley finished with 115 yards and two touchdowns on 16 carries.

Luke Moga was surgical, 19 of 26 for 248 yards and three touchdowns. Two of them went to Bailen George, both from 17 yards, and George finished with six catches for 100 yards. Tripp Walsh caught the last one with 1:58 left to make it 42-19.

Air Force hung around until Evan Medders scored in the third quarter and fumbled the two-point try, leaving it 21-19. Then Sibley scored again and Moga hit George again, and the Falcons were done. The Lobos scored the last 21 points of the night.

This defense is a wrecking crew. Swaim made 12 tackles. Tavian Combs intercepted a throw. Nine more tackles for loss pushed our single-season record to 101, blowing past the old mark of 90, and we have 30 takeaways, the most for this program in 36 years.

We're 10-2, 7-1 in the Mountain West, and the conference title game is at our place next Friday. Bring your loudest howl, bring the green chile, and bring a friend. Go Lobos.

articles.title: San José State vs North Dakota State: Clark Shines in Defeat, 31-38
articles.byline: Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz, The San José State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: North Dakota State Bison (10-2) 38, San José State Spartans (5-8) 31, Fri., Nov. 27, CEFCU Stadium, San Jose. Regular season complete
articles.text:
San José State fell 38-31 to North Dakota State in our home finale, and the season ends at 5-8. The last snap came from the Bison 4, with four seconds left. I'll be seeing that one in my sleep.

Carson Clark was the best player on the field for us. Thirteen catches, 137 yards, two touchdowns, including a 3-yard grab in the first quarter and a 7-yarder with 9:52 left that made it 38-31. Jerry McClure piled on 117 receiving yards. Luke Weaver threw for 306 yards and ran one in from the 5 to open the fourth quarter. When this offense got going, it was fun to watch.

The trouble came early and late. NDSU scored 17 straight in the first half, and Ray James Jr. returned a Weaver interception 14 yards for a touchdown in the third. We were down 31-14 and fighting uphill all night.

Still, the Spartans clawed back. Isaiah Carlson scored before halftime. Trajan Sinatra kicked a 30-yarder. Weaver and Clark kept answering. Then came the last drive: 43 seconds, all the way to the red zone, a pre-snap flag that cost us five yards, and an interception at the 4 to end it.

Dominique McKenzie gave us a jolt with a 57-yard kickoff return. Isaiah Buxton grabbed an interception, and Brian Dukes Jr. made eight tackles. We held the Bison to 5 of 16 on third down.

Three interceptions and 26 completions on 50 throws were too much to overcome against a team that wins like NDSU does. The Bison won 10 games in their first FBS season for a reason, and Friday showed us why.

We finish 5-8, and the offseason begins tonight. It will be a long one, and every one of us will spend it replaying four seconds at the Bison 4. Clark, McClure and Weaver gave this city a reason to believe the offense is close. Spartan Up.

articles.title: North Dakota State vs San José State: Brown's Debut Makes 10, 38-31
articles.byline: Ingeborg 'Inga' Halvorsen, The North Dakota State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: North Dakota State Bison (10-2) 38, San José State Spartans (5-8) 31, Fri., Nov. 27, CEFCU Stadium, San Jose. Regular season complete
articles.text:
Ten wins in our first season of FBS football. Let that sink in, Bison Nation. North Dakota State beat San José State 38-31 at CEFCU Stadium on Black Friday, and a quarterback in his first game as the No. 1 guy got us there.

Preston Brown got the call in place of Nathan Hayes for his first career nod, and on our first drive he uncorked a 49-yard touchdown to Jackson Williams. Welcome to the job, kid. Brown finished 12 of 23 for 226 yards, and when the Spartans cut it to 31-24 early in the fourth quarter, he answered with a 5-yard touchdown run to make it 38-24. That's poise you can't teach.

Williams was terrific, seven catches for 117 yards. DJ Scott punched in two short touchdowns in a span of less than three minutes across the first and second quarters, and he finished with 86 rushing yards. Drew Klein's 31-yard field goal made it 24-7, and we looked ready to cruise.

Then the defense did what this defense does. Ray James Jr. stepped in front of a Luke Weaver throw and returned it 14 yards to the end zone in the third quarter, 31-14. That's the sixth defensive touchdown for the Bison this season. Gavin Sell and Jaylen Archibald added interceptions, and Sell's came at our 4 with four seconds left to end it. San José State reached the red zone on that last drive and came away empty.

I'll admit the Spartans made it nervous. Weaver threw for 306 yards, and Carson Clark caught 13 balls. We committed 11 penalties for 85 yards, and that has to get fixed before December.

But 10-2 is 10-2. Now we wait to see whether the Mountain West championship game is in our future. Whatever comes next, this first FBS season already belongs in the trophy case next to all the others in Fargo. Go Bison.

articles.title: Memphis vs Temple: A 17-Point Fourth-Quarter Lead Slips Away, 31-35
articles.byline: Otis Delaney-Crum, The Memphis Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Temple Owls (3-9) 35, Memphis Tigers (8-4) 31, Fri., Nov. 27, Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium, Memphis. Regular season complete
articles.text:
I don't have words for this, so I'll use numbers. Memphis led Temple 31-14 after three quarters at Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium. Final: Temple 35, Memphis 31. The Owls came in 2-9. And our chance at the conference title game probably went with it.

For three quarters, the Tigers looked like a team ready for December. Marcus Stokes hit Stonka Burnside for a 39-yard touchdown on the opening drive. Jaylin Carter ran in from 4 and from 3. Jemyri Davis took a Stokes throw 41 yards to the end zone early in the third. Burnside finished with 117 yards on five catches, and Carter ran 21 times for 103 yards. Stokes averaged 13.7 yards a throw.

Then it all came apart. Pinned deep after a great Temple punt, Stokes threw an interception that Saboor Karriem took back for six barely a minute into the fourth. Temple went 94 yards in 16 plays to make it 31-28. And with 1:45 left, holding the lead, Stokes threw a second interception on third-and-13. Jaxon Smolik drove the Owls 55 yards and found JoJo Bermudez for the winner with 13 seconds left.

Three turnovers. Temple held the ball for 34:38 and converted 9 of 16 on third down. Our defense, which had played well for three quarters, was gassed by the end.

Credit where it's due on our side: Mike Montgomery made 12 tackles, and Beni Mwamba returned an interception 48 yards. Those guys deserved a better ending.

We're 8-4, 5-3 in the American. We needed a win and a North Texas loss to reach the title game against UTSA. Now we wait on Saturday's results and the computer rankings, and I can't bear to look. Whatever bowl comes, this team owes our home crowd of 30,610 a better final quarter than the one they sat through Friday. Go Tigers Go.

articles.title: Temple vs Memphis: Owls Erase 17 in the Fourth, Stun Tigers, 35-31
articles.byline: Teddy Fiorella, The Temple Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Temple Owls (3-9) 35, Memphis Tigers (8-4) 31, Fri., Nov. 27, Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium, Memphis. Regular season complete
articles.text:
Thirteen seconds left. Jaxon Smolik to JoJo Bermudez, 11 yards, touchdown. Temple 35, Memphis 31, and my voice is gone from North Broad Street to the Delaware River. The Owls were down 31-14 when the fourth quarter began at Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium. They won anyway.

This comeback had layers. First, Dante Atton dropped a punt inside the Memphis 5. On the very next snap, Saboor Karriem jumped a Marcus Stokes throw and took it 10 yards for a touchdown, 61 seconds into the quarter. 31-21. Then De'Carlos Young capped a 16-play, 94-yard march with a 4-yard touchdown run, and it was 31-28 with 7:03 to go.

Memphis still had the ball and the lead with two minutes to play, and we needed one more miracle. We got it. Then Jaeden Gould intercepted Stokes on third-and-13 and brought it back 26 yards to our 45 with 1:45 left. Smolik took off for 19 yards on third-and-10. He hit Young for 11. Then Bermudez, in the end zone, with 13 seconds on the clock. Six straight losses, gone in a blink.

Smolik was gutsy all night: 20 of 34 for 200 yards, plus 54 rushing yards and a 1-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Young carried 16 times for 94 yards and two scores. Curly Ordonez made 14 tackles. We converted 9 of 16 third downs and held the ball for 34:38.

Yes, we finish 3-9, 2-6 in the American. Yes, this season tested every one of us. But the last memory of 2026 is the Owls walking off a field in Memphis with a win that probably knocked the Tigers out of the conference title race.

That's the kind of finish you build on. A team that never stopped fighting in a lost season gives you a reason to believe come August. Bring on next year. T for Temple U.

articles.title: Florida State vs Florida: Short-Handed Noles Fall at Doak, 10-26
articles.byline: Gianna Ravello, The Florida State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Florida Gators (8-4) 26, Florida State Seminoles (5-7) 10, Fri., Nov. 27, Doak Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee. Regular season complete
articles.text:
The Gators came to our house and left with a 26-10 win, and Florida State's season ends at 5-7. Three straight losses to the Gators. I'll say it plainly: that stings worse than the record.

We had our moments. Micahi Danzy turned a short catch into a 64-yard gallop in the second quarter, and Gabe Panikowski's 27-yard field goal made it 7-3. Down 17-3 in the third, Kevin Sperry came in for a series and threw a 9-yard touchdown to Landen Thomas on fourth down. That made it 17-10, and for a few minutes Doak believed.

Then Patrick Durkin kicked three field goals in the fourth quarter, and that was the ballgame. We couldn't flip the field all day; our punts averaged 32.9 yards, and the defense kept defending short fields. Ashton Daniels was 18 of 32 for 183 yards and threw two interceptions. We went 5 of 17 on third down.

We were down to our fifth running back, and Zay Parks still gave us 55 yards on 14 carries. That tells you about the kid. Jasen Lopez caught seven balls. Nehemiah Chandler intercepted Tramell Jones Jr. in the fourth quarter, and K.J. Kirkland made eight tackles.

Here's the part I want to remember: Rick Stockstill stepped in as interim coach after Mike Norvell was dismissed on Nov. 1, and this group went 2-2 the rest of the way. They didn't quit, even shorthanded, even with the Gators chasing a third straight rivalry win.

The defense held Florida to 282 yards and 10 first downs. That's a group that deserved more help.

Now comes a long offseason and a coaching search that will shape the next few years of this program. The Gators have had their run, three straight. Streaks end. Ours against them will begin somewhere, and I want it to be next November. Go Noles.

articles.title: Florida vs Florida State: Baugh Makes History in Tallahassee, 26-10
articles.byline: Dax Marchetti, The Florida Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Florida Gators (8-4) 26, Florida State Seminoles (5-7) 10, Fri., Nov. 27, Doak Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee. Regular season complete
articles.text:
Three in a row against the Seminoles. Say it louder for the folks in Tallahassee. Florida went into Doak Campbell Stadium on Black Friday, beat Florida State 26-10 in front of 67,277, and Jadan Baugh wrote his name into Gator history while he was at it.

Baugh got us on the board with a 3-yard touchdown run late in the first quarter, and somewhere in that first half he crossed 1,000 rushing yards for the season. That makes him the first Florida tailback ever with back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons. He finished with 77 yards on 19 carries and sits at 1,057 for the year with a bowl game still to come.

Aaron Philo was sharp before he left the game, 9 of 12 for 127 yards. He hit Eric Singleton Jr. on a 65-yard strike down to the Florida State 7 in the first quarter, and his 37-yard scramble in the third set up Tramell Jones Jr., who came in and plunged in from the 1 to make it 17-3. Jones signed with Florida after committing to Florida State, so you know that one felt good. The Seminoles answered on a fourth-down touchdown throw, 17-10, and then Patrick Durkin went to work.

Durkin was perfect: 33, 37, 42 and 25 yards. Four kicks, four makes, 14 points. Every time Florida State thought it had a pulse, Durkin pushed the margin back to double digits. Give that man a parking spot.

And the defense was nasty. Jayden Woods had three sacks. Three! J'Vari Flowers intercepted Ashton Daniels twice. Myles Graham made 12 tackles. We forced seven punts and held the Seminoles to 98 rushing yards on 37 carries.

We're 8-4. A year ago this program was 4-8. Jon Sumrall's first team flipped the record, won its last three, and owns this rivalry again, six wins in the last eight meetings. We'll learn the bowl destination on Dec. 6, and I'm already shopping for orange and blue. Go Gators.

articles.byline: Zebulon 'Zeb' Coldiron, The App State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: South Alabama Jaguars (7-5) 20, App State Mountaineers (7-5) 13, Fri., Nov. 27, Hancock Whitney Stadium, Mobile. Regular season complete
articles.text:
App State lost 20-13 at South Alabama on Friday, and I keep replaying two interceptions in the end zone and one fourth-and-inches run that went nowhere. Three trips that could have changed the night in Mobile, and we came away with zero points and a heartache.

We dug out of a 10-0 hole with real grit. Jaquari Lewis plunged in from the 1 in the second quarter, and James London hit field goals from 42 and 29 yards. When London's second kick went through with 6:49 left in the third, we led 13-10, and the Mountaineers had the Jaguars on their heels.

Then the fourth quarter. Malachi Singleton threw an interception in the end zone early in the quarter. Next drive, with the score tied at 13, we went for it on fourth-and-inches, and Lewis got stopped for no gain with 5:44 left. South Alabama marched 73 yards and scored with 1:46 to go. We had one more chance, and Singleton's final throw died in a Jaguar's arms in the end zone in the closing seconds.

It hurts more because we played well for long stretches. Singleton completed 22 of 28 throws for 240 yards. Darrin Fugitt caught five for 79, and Chris Lofton and Nate Branch kept the chains moving. Lewis carried 25 times for 93 yards and our touchdown. We had more first downs, 23 to 15, and held the ball for 31:05. Colton Phares made eight tackles, and Devin Henderson came up with an interception of his own.

But you can't leave points at the doorstep twice in one quarter and expect to win on the road in this league.

We finish the regular season 7-5, 5-3 in league play, with a bowl bid likely. One more game in black and gold sounds good to me, and this group earned it. Go Apps.

articles.title: South Alabama vs App State: Two End-Zone Interceptions Win It, 20-13
articles.byline: Azalea Fairhope-Grice, The South Alabama Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: South Alabama Jaguars (7-5) 20, App State Mountaineers (7-5) 13, Fri., Nov. 27, Hancock Whitney Stadium, Mobile. Regular season complete
articles.text:
Two interceptions in our own end zone, one fourth-down stuff, and one 73-yard drive. That's the recipe South Alabama used to beat App State 20-13 on Black Friday at Hancock Whitney Stadium, and Mobile is going to sleep happy.

We jumped out fast. Bishop Davenport hit Everett Hunter for a 6-yard touchdown in the first quarter, and Dylan Freebury tacked on a 21-yard field goal for a 10-0 lead. Then App State spent the next two quarters chipping away with a touchdown and two James London field goals, and we trailed 13-10 in the third. Freebury tied it from 34 with 1:04 left in the quarter.

This is where the defense took the game. Kam Robinson intercepted Malachi Singleton in the end zone early in the fourth. On App State's next drive, the Mountaineers went for it on fourth-and-inches, and we stuffed Jaquari Lewis for no gain with 5:44 left. That stop gave the ball back to Davenport, and he went to work.

Eleven plays. Seventy-three yards. Keenan Phillips finished it with a 7-yard touchdown run with 1:46 left, and it was 20-13. App State drove one last time, and Jayvon Henderson chose the perfect moment for an interception in the end zone in the closing seconds. Ballgame, Jaguars.

Davenport was 15 of 25 for 211 yards and a touchdown, and he ran for 40 more. Anthony Eager caught four balls for 72 yards. Camen Upshaw was everywhere with 14 tackles and a sack, and Masey Lewis added a sack and a half.

The Mountaineers held the ball longer and had more first downs, but we had the two biggest defensive plays of the night, and both came with our backs against the wall.

We're 7-5, 5-3 in the Sun Belt, and bowl season is next. This defense earned every one of those seven wins. Jag Up, Mobile.

articles.title: Ohio vs Toledo: Levi Davis Rallies Us, Rockets Win at the Gun, 31-34
articles.byline: Penny Trautman, The Ohio Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Toledo Rockets (10-2) 34, Ohio Bobcats (8-4) 31, Fri., Nov. 27, Peden Stadium, Athens. Regular season complete
articles.text:
Ohio lost 34-31 to Toledo on a field goal with no time left at Peden Stadium, and I'm going to need the whole weekend. We were down 17-0. We came back. We led. And then 44 seconds broke my heart.

Let's talk about Levi Davis, because the freshman deserves the headline. He came on for Nick Poulos midway through the second quarter with us trailing 17-0 and went 17 of 28 for 288 yards. His first drive ended in a field goal. His second ended in the end zone. He found Riley Neer for a 16-yard touchdown with eight seconds left in the half, ran in from the 1 to tie it at 17 in the third, and broke a 23-yard touchdown run with 4:55 left that gave us a 31-24 lead. Seventy rushing yards and two scores on the ground, too. Athens has a new hero, and he's only a freshman.

Preston Bowman caught eight balls for 150 yards. Dom Dorwart caught seven for 120. Victor Rosa plowed in from the 1 to tie it at 24. We piled up 458 yards, and for most of the second half the Bobcats looked like the better team.

Then the ending. Toledo tied it at 31 with 1:33 left. We went three-and-out. A punt return, a facemask penalty, seven plays, and Reice Griffith hit from 22 as the clock ran out. I've watched a lot of Ohio football. Few losses felt as cruel as this one. A three-and-out with the game tied is the snap I'll replay all winter.

Darren James-Hamilton and Charlie Christopher each made 10 tackles, and Kendall Bannister recovered a fumble. Toledo still ran for 226 yards, and that's where the game slipped away.

We're 8-4, 6-2 in the MAC, and a bowl invitation should be coming. Davis gives this program a reason to circle next August already. Stand Up and Cheer.

articles.title: Toledo vs Ohio: Griffith at the Gun Sends Rockets to Detroit, 34-31
articles.byline: Rocco Szczepanski, The Toledo Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Toledo Rockets (10-2) 34, Ohio Bobcats (8-4) 31, Fri., Nov. 27, Peden Stadium, Athens. Next: at Buffalo, Sat., Dec. 5, 12:00 PM ET, Ford Field, Detroit
articles.text:
Forty-four seconds. That's all Toledo needed to turn a tie game into a trip to Ford Field. Reice Griffith knocked through a 22-yard field goal as time expired at Peden Stadium, the Rockets beat Ohio 34-31, and we're playing Buffalo for the MAC championship on Dec. 5.

We came out on fire. John Alan Richter hit Bryson Hammer for a 43-yard touchdown, then found Adjatay Dabbs for 24 more, and Griffith tacked on a 33-yard field goal early in the second quarter. Toledo 17, Ohio 0. I was already pricing gas to Detroit.

Then Ohio woke up. The Bobcats scored 17 straight, and a freshman named Levi Davis ran in from 23 yards out with 4:55 left to give them a 31-24 lead. My stomach hit the floor in Athens.

Here's why I love this team. CJ Miller, who had already scored from 12 yards out to open the fourth quarter, punched in a 5-yard touchdown with 1:33 left to tie it at 31. Our defense forced a three-and-out. Hammer returned the punt 9 yards to our 30, a facemask flag added 15 more, and Richter moved us 65 yards in seven plays. Griffith did the rest. Ballgame. Bedlam.

Miller finished with 109 yards and two touchdowns on 15 carries, and Connor Walendzak added 80. We ran for 226 yards as a team. Richter was 18 of 31 for 211 yards and two scores with no interceptions. Nicholas Thompson made 13 tackles, and Tyrell Russell grabbed an interception.

Fair is fair: we gave up 458 yards, and Ohio's receivers had big days. We'll need to tighten that up before Buffalo, because the Bulls just ground out a title-game berth of their own at Akron. Two MAC heavyweights, one trophy, one Saturday in Detroit.

At 10-2 and 7-1 in league play, the Glass City is headed to Detroit. Rocket up.

articles.title: Akron vs Buffalo: Zips Push the Title-Bound Bulls to the End, 9-17
articles.byline: Hollister 'Zip' Grubbs, The Akron Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Buffalo Bulls (9-3) 17, Akron Zips (2-10) 9, Fri., Nov. 27, InfoCision Stadium, Akron. Regular season complete
articles.text:
Akron lost 17-9 to Buffalo at InfoCision Stadium, and for three quarters the Zips gave a team headed to the MAC title game all it could handle.

Down 7-0 late in the half, Cibastian Broughton found Miles Burris for an 18-yard touchdown with 40 seconds left. We missed the extra point, but a one-point halftime deficit had our sideline alive. Matthew Schramm came out in the third and drilled a 50-yard field goal, and we led 9-7. The Rubber City had a lead on a holiday weekend.

Then Buffalo kicked a 39-yarder to go back up 10-9 with 2:25 left in the third. We answered with an 11-play drive deep into Bulls territory, and that's where it went sideways. A holding call backed us up, and Schramm missed from 39. Messiah Burch broke a 43-yard touchdown run not long after, and that was the ballgame.

Kyan Mason was a problem for them all day, four catches for 95 yards. Jordan Gant ground out 72 yards on 20 carries. Dwight Nunoo made 12 tackles, and Jalen Williams had three tackles for loss. We didn't lose the ball once and outgained Buffalo 304 to 235. That's how close this was.

But 3 of 12 on third down will cost you, and so will one missed kick in a one-score game. We had the Bulls right where we wanted them and let them off the hook.

We finish 2-10, 1-7 in the MAC. After the game, Joe Moorhead announced on social media that he's stepping down after five seasons, so a new chapter begins in Akron. The guys who fought Buffalo to the final quarter deserve a coach who builds on that.

Hold on to Mason. Hold on to Nunoo. Hold on to the fight these guys showed on the last Friday of the season. Go Zips.

articles.title: Buffalo vs Akron: Burch Bulls Into the MAC Title Game, 17-9
articles.byline: Kendra Woolcott, The Buffalo Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Buffalo Bulls (9-3) 17, Akron Zips (2-10) 9, Fri., Nov. 27, InfoCision Stadium, Akron. Next: vs Toledo, Sat., Dec. 5, 12:00 PM ET, Ford Field, Detroit
articles.text:
Pack for Detroit, Bulls fans. Buffalo grinded out a 17-9 win at Akron on Black Friday, and the reward is a date with Toledo for the MAC championship at Ford Field on Saturday, Dec. 5.

This one was not pretty, and I don't care one bit. Messiah Burch carried us. He ran 24 times for 130 yards, and with 9:58 left he took a handoff 43 yards to the end zone to make it 17-9. That run felt like a door slamming on the Zips' season.

We needed it, because Akron made us sweat at InfoCision Stadium. Jason Wright found Terrance Shelton Jr. for a 21-yard touchdown midway through the second quarter, but the Zips answered with an 18-yard score just before halftime. Akron missed the extra point, so it was 7-6 at the break. Then Matthew Schramm hit a 50-yarder in the third, and for the first time all day we were chasing, 9-7.

Enter Oliver Hautanen. His 39-yard field goal with 2:25 left in the third gave us a 10-9 lead we never gave back. Akron drove deep into our end early in the fourth, a holding flag pushed the Zips back, and Schramm missed from 39. Burch went 43 yards not long after, and the Bulls were headed to Detroit.

Wright only completed 8 of 18 throws for 88 yards, so this was a ground-and-defense day, and that's fine by me. SaVeon Brown made nine tackles, and the defense held the Zips to 112 rushing yards. We had zero turnovers, only two penalties, and we went 2 for 2 on fourth down. Chance Morrow caught four balls for 36 yards.

We're 9-3, 7-1 in the MAC, and the conference title is one win away. Toledo beat Ohio on a walk-off kick the same afternoon, so Ford Field gets two teams that know how to finish close games. Go Bulls.

articles.title: Tulsa vs UTSA: Hayes Fights to the End in San Antonio, 22-28
articles.byline: Wiley Pettibone, The Tulsa Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: UTSA Roadrunners (10-2) 28, Tulsa Golden Hurricane (7-5) 22, Fri., Nov. 27, Alamodome, San Antonio. Regular season complete
articles.text:
Tulsa lost 28-22 at UTSA on Friday afternoon, and if you turned it off at halftime, shame on you. Down 25-7 at the Alamodome, the Golden Hurricane kept swinging until the clock said stop.

The early going was rough. UTSA hit a 64-yard touchdown on its first drive. Baylor Hayes answered right away, dropping a 38-yard touchdown to Jimmy Calloway to tie it at 7. Then the Roadrunners went deep again for 79 yards. Calloway finished with 84 yards on three catches, and he looked like the fastest man in Texas on that score.

The second quarter is the one I'll be forgetting on purpose. We fumbled at our own 1 and had to fall on it in the end zone for a safety, Hayes got sacked in the end zone for another, and UTSA added a short touchdown before the half. Two safeties in one quarter. I didn't know that was legal.

Ten wins, seven in league play, and the next game is a title game at home. Birds Up, San Antonio.

articles.title: Nebraska vs Iowa: Rule Runs Hard, Huskers Fall at Kinnick, 7-31
articles.byline: Darla Rasmussen, The Nebraska Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Iowa Hawkeyes (10-2) 31, Nebraska Cornhuskers (7-5) 7, Fri., Nov. 27, Kinnick Stadium, Iowa City. Regular season complete
articles.text:
Six days after we beat Ohio State 31-28, Nebraska walked into Kinnick Stadium the day after Thanksgiving and left with a 31-7 loss to Iowa. I've been a Husker fan long enough to know that a week can feel like a decade.

Jamal Rule did his part. He carried 18 times for 106 yards, and his 21-yard touchdown run early in the second quarter tied it at 7. For a while that was a fistfight, and we were throwing punches.

Then came the third quarter, and the play I'll be stewing on until spring. Trailing 10-7, Jamir Conn recovered a muffed Iowa punt and handed us a short field. We drove to the Iowa 35. Fourth down. No. The Hawkeyes took the ball back, Hank Brown went down and scored from the 6, and it was 17-7. That was the swing, right there.

After that, the wheels came off. Anthony Colandrea was 19 of 29 for 153 yards with an interception, and he and Jacory Barney Jr. each lost a fumble. Three turnovers on the road against the best scoring defense in the country is a recipe for exactly this. Brown ran for three touchdowns and threw for another, and Iowa outgained us 329-260. Nobody had done that to us all season.

Some of our guys played their hearts out. Danny Odem III made 10 tackles. Dwayne McDougle III got home for a sack. Luke Lindenmeyer caught six balls for 63 yards. We only had two penalties all afternoon.

But 1 of 3 on fourth down and 4 of 12 on third down doesn't beat Iowa in Iowa City.

We're 7-5, 4-5 in the Big Ten, and we'll learn our bowl destination soon. Seven wins, a takedown of Ohio State and a bowl trip is a season worth defending at any diner in the state. We'll be back for the Hawkeyes next November. GBR.

articles.title: Iowa vs Nebraska: Hank Brown Runs Wild at Kinnick, 31-7
articles.byline: Orrin Kalvelage, The Iowa Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Iowa Hawkeyes (10-2) 31, Nebraska Cornhuskers (7-5) 7, Fri., Nov. 27, Kinnick Stadium, Iowa City. Regular season complete
articles.text:
Ten wins. Say it slowly, Hawkeye fans, because Iowa just beat Nebraska 31-7 on Black Friday in front of 69,250 at Kinnick Stadium, and that's five straight wins for a team nobody wants to see in December.

Hank Brown was the story. Our quarterback ran for three touchdowns and threw for another, and he did it with the kind of legs I didn't know he had in August. He opened the scoring from 14 yards out in the first quarter, scored from the 6 late in the third for a 17-7 lead, and put the bow on it with a 29-yard run with 4:02 left. Through the air he was 13 of 18 for 173 yards, including a 9-yard touchdown to DJ Vonnahme that made it 24-7 early in the fourth.

Nebraska hung around for a while. Jamal Rule ripped off a 21-yard touchdown run to tie it at 7 early in the second quarter, and Caden Buhr's 39-yard field goal was all that separated us at the half. Then the Huskers recovered a muffed punt in the third quarter, trailing 10-7, and drove to our 35. Our defense said no on fourth down, and Brown went right down the field and scored on the next possession. Ballgame.

And the defense. Oh, the defense. Cam Buffington made 12 tackles and recovered a fumble. Jayden Montgomery had 11 tackles, a sack and two tackles for loss. Jaylen Watson grabbed an interception, and Brevin Doll fell on another loose ball. Three Nebraska turnovers, zero second-half points, and the third straight game we've blanked somebody after halftime.

L.J. Phillips Jr. chipped in 76 yards on 14 carries, and we outgained Nebraska 329-260, the first time anybody has done that to them all season.

That's 11 wins in the last 12 against the Huskers. In this five-game streak we've outscored people 147-41.

We're 10-2, 7-2 in the Big Ten, and what comes next is out of our hands. Whatever the committee decides, this team put it on tape. Go Hawks.

articles.title: Mississippi State vs Ole Miss: Three Points Away in Oxford, 17-41
articles.byline: Wade Pettus, The Mississippi State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Ole Miss Rebels (8-4) 41, Mississippi State Bulldogs (5-7) 17, Fri., Nov. 27, Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, Oxford. Regular season complete
articles.text:
For one half in Oxford, Mississippi State owned the Egg Bowl. We went to the locker room up 10-6, Fluff Bothwell was running through the Rebels like they owed him money, and Kyle Ferrie had just drilled a 42-yard field goal with 1:48 left in the half. The final says Ole Miss 41-17. I'd like a word with the third quarter.

Bothwell was the best player on that field. He went 16 yards for our first touchdown, finished with 129 yards on 18 carries, and caught three balls, including the 12-yard touchdown from Parker Puckett on the first play of the fourth quarter that cut it to 20-17. Puckett was sharp all night, 22 of 27 for 201 yards, and Marquis Johnson hauled in five catches for 96 yards, one of them a 45-yarder.

We had the Rebels sweating. Down three, driving, momentum on our side. Then Blake Purchase jumped a Puckett throw and ran it back 58 yards to our 1. Trinidad Chambliss walked in on the next snap, and it went from 20-17 to 27-17 in about the time it takes to say Egg Bowl.

From there, Ole Miss scored twice more, and the 35-7 second half makes this look like a blowout it wasn't for 30 minutes. We held the ball for 33:22. Jardin Gilbert made nine tackles and a sack. Fatt Forrest added eight tackles and Kendel Dolby seven.

But you can't give a team like that 10 penalties for 84 yards and expect to survive Oxford, and a 3-of-11 night on third down will not get it done either.

We finish 5-7, 2-7 in the SEC, and the season ends with a trophy we wanted sitting on the wrong side of the state. One more win and we'd be packing for a bowl. That's the part that stings tonight.

Here's the part I'm keeping: the first half, Bothwell's legs and Puckett's poise. Our cowbells will be loud again next November. Hail State.

articles.title: Ole Miss vs Mississippi State: Purchase Flips the Egg Bowl, 41-17
articles.byline: Langston Fairbanks, The Ole Miss Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Ole Miss Rebels (8-4) 41, Mississippi State Bulldogs (5-7) 17, Fri., Nov. 27, Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, Oxford. Regular season complete
articles.text:
Halftime in Oxford, and the scoreboard at Vaught-Hemingway said Mississippi State 10, Ole Miss 6. I heard a few boos from our own side when the two-minute drill fizzled and Lucas Carneiro's 62-yard try fell short. By the final gun it was 41-17, and the Egg Bowl belongs to us for the fourth year in a row.

The second half was 35-7, and Trinidad Chambliss ran the show. He hit Horatio Fields for a 6-yard touchdown with 9:53 left in the third for our first lead, 13-10. Joshua Dye bulled in from the 4 to make it 20-10. Chambliss finished 23 of 36 for 237 yards, two touchdown throws and a touchdown run.

Give State credit for one punch. Parker Puckett found Fluff Bothwell for a 12-yard score on the first snap of the fourth quarter, and it was 20-17 with the Bulldogs driving again. Then Blake Purchase stepped in front of a Puckett throw and ran 58 yards the other way, all the way to the State 1. Chambliss went around left end on the next play, and it was 27-17 with 10:30 to go. That interception was the whole night in one snap.

After that, the floodgates. Chambliss found Michael Smith for 21 yards and a touchdown, and Dye punched in his second score from a yard out with 1:57 left. Dye carried 20 times for 91 yards on a night our ground game needed somebody to grab it.

The defense got meaner as the night went on. Tah'j Butler made 10 tackles and a sack, and Suntarine Perkins had 1.5 sacks and three tackles for loss. We went 8 of 13 on third down and didn't lose the ball once.

Honest notes for the film room: Bothwell ran for 129 yards on 18 carries, and State had the ball for 33:22. We were sloppy for two quarters. We were also the better team for two quarters, and that was plenty.

That's four straight Egg Bowls and six of the last seven. We're 8-4, 5-4 in the SEC, waiting on a bowl invitation, and the trophy stays in Oxford for another year. Hotty Toddy.

articles.title: Buffalo Bills vs Kansas City Chiefs Week 12: Bass From 57, 13-10
articles.matchup: Final: Buffalo Bills (10-1) 13, Kansas City Chiefs (8-3) 10, Thu., Nov. 26, Highmark Stadium, Orchard Park. Next: at New England Patriots, Sun., Dec. 6, 4:25 PM ET, Gillette Stadium, Foxborough
articles.text:
Buffalo Bills 13, Kansas City Chiefs 10, and Tyler Bass ended Thanksgiving night with a 57-yard field goal as the clock hit zero in Orchard Park. That morning, more than 14,000 runners took the 131st YMCA Turkey Trot through downtown Buffalo on a brand-new loop that begins and ends at the Buffalo Convention Center, and Christopher Bertola of Orchard Park won it in 24:14. Orchard Park went two for two today.

This one was a grind, and James Cook III carried it. Thirty-two carries, 117 yards and the only Buffalo touchdown. His 3-yard run into the end zone got overturned on review at the 1, a pre-snap flag pushed us back to the 5, and he went 5 yards on the next snap anyway for 7-0 early in the second quarter.

Josh Allen had a rough night throwing, 10 of 21 for 81 yards and two interceptions, one in the end zone and one at the Kansas City 13. He kept us moving with his legs, 43 yards on seven carries, but we left points out there.

The defense won this game. Kansas City got 241 yards. Greg Rousseau sacked Patrick Mahomes and hit him three times. After Emmett Johnson's 1-yard touchdown put the Chiefs up 10-7, Terrel Bernard, Cole Bishop and Davison Igbinosun made sure they never scored again. Bass tied it from 54 with 11:58 left, and Harrison Butker missed from 46 with 6:01 to go.

Then the punters took the stage. Tommy Doman Jr. dropped one at the Kansas City 2 with 2:11 left, and the Chiefs went three-and-out after a Rashee Rice catch on third down was reversed on review. After Kansas City punted again from its own end with 15 seconds left, Greg Dortch returned it 17 yards to the Kansas City 39. One snap, 57 yards, ballgame.

That's seven straight wins, and we're 10-1. Next we visit the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on Sunday, Dec. 6, at 4:25 PM ET, and they're the last team to beat us. Bertola needed 24 minutes and change to win his race Thursday morning. Bass needed one kick. Go Bills.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys vs Philadelphia Eagles Week 12: Lead Lost, 38-39
articles.matchup: Final: Philadelphia Eagles (4-7) 39, Dallas Cowboys (5-7) 38, Thu., Nov. 26, AT&T Stadium, Arlington. Next: at Seattle Seahawks, Mon., Dec. 7, 8:15 PM ET, Lumen Field, Seattle
articles.text:
The Philadelphia Eagles beat the Dallas Cowboys 39-38 at AT&T Stadium on Thanksgiving, and we led by 21 in the third quarter. Miranda Lambert walked out at halftime for the 30th Salvation Army Red Kettle Kickoff, with a giant disco ball hanging above the stage and the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders around her, and we were up 28-10. She sang "Kerosene." The second half went up in flames.

Javonte Williams owned the first half. He scored from the 1 to finish an 11-play opening drive, ran in from 12 in the second quarter, and caught a 12-yarder from Dak Prescott with four seconds left before the break. KaVontae Turpin took a short throw 31 yards to the end zone, and Brandon Aubrey hit a 59-yarder in the third for 31-10.

Then it came apart one piece at a time. DeVonta Smith beat us for 45 yards. We took a delay of game on fourth down, the Eagles blocked Bryan Anger's punt, and Kenny Moore II recovered at our 3 for a touchdown. Prescott scrambled 14 yards to make it 38-24, and Britain Covey answered with a 55-yard kickoff return that set up a Joe Milton touchdown run. Cobie Durant intercepted Milton with 7:14 left, and the game was still in our hands.

Two moments will stay with me all winter. Aubrey, who had already made one from 59, missed a 40-yarder wide left with 3:27 to go. After the Eagles scored to make it 38-36, we faced fourth-and-1 at their 39 with 55 seconds left and went for it. Ty Robinson sacked Prescott for a 9-yard loss. Jake Elliott made a 59-yarder with two seconds left, and Andrew Mukuba intercepted our final heave.

There was good football in there. Prescott threw for 291 yards and two scores and ran for a third. CeeDee Lamb caught seven balls for 134 yards. Williams carried 29 times for 101 yards. Quinnen Williams and Shemar James each got to Milton for a sack. And 93,417 people packed the building to watch it slip away.

We're 5-7, and the Seattle Seahawks host us at Lumen Field on Monday, Dec. 7, at 8:15 PM ET. Short of a miracle, December is about pride now. The Red Kettles are out on every corner in Dallas, and I'm dropping a few dollars in one on the way home, because somebody in this town should end Thanksgiving feeling good.

articles.text:
Philadelphia Eagles 39, Dallas Cowboys 38, and Jake Elliott won it from 59 yards with two seconds left in Arlington. In Philadelphia, the Thanksgiving Day Parade on the Benjamin Franklin Parkway, the oldest in the country going back to 1920, got called off Wednesday night because of a high wind warning. Philly lost its parade, so the Birds held one in Texas.

Nobody was planning a parade at halftime. Dallas led 28-10. Javonte Williams had two touchdown runs and a 12-yard touchdown catch with four seconds left in the half, and Brandon Aubrey made it 31-10 with a 59-yarder in the third. Our one bright spot was DeVonta Smith, who took a Joe Milton throw 50 yards for a score in the second quarter.

Smith did it again with 15 seconds left in the third, 45 yards for 17-31. Then Ty Robinson got a hand on a Bryan Anger punt, and Kenny Moore II scooped it at the Dallas 3 and carried it in. Dak Prescott answered with a 14-yard scramble for 38-24, and Britain Covey brought the kickoff back 55 yards. Three snaps later, Milton ran it in from 15 himself. The two-point try failed, and it was 30-38.

Milton gave one away when Cobie Durant intercepted him with 7:14 left, but the defense held, and Aubrey pushed a 40-yarder wide left at 3:27. Milton went 70 yards in four plays: Darius Cooper for 14, Elijah Moore for 23 and 9, and Makai Lemon for a 24-yard touchdown. A holding flag erased a good two-point try, and the second try fell incomplete. 36-38.

Then Dallas went for it on fourth-and-1 at our 39 with 55 seconds left, and Robinson buried Prescott for a 9-yard sack. We had the ball at our 48 with 50 seconds to play. Smith caught one for 9, a Dallas interference flag gave us 2 more, Smith grabbed another for 5, and Elliott walked out and hit from 59. Andrew Mukuba intercepted the last heave for good measure.

Smith caught 11 balls for 200 yards and two scores. Milton threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. made 12 tackles, and Robinson finished with a blocked punt and the sack that flipped the game. We scored 22 points in the fourth quarter.

That's two straight wins, and we're 4-7 with the Arizona Cardinals next at State Farm Stadium, Sunday, Dec. 6, at 4:05 PM ET. The Parkway can have its floats back next year. On Thursday, the parade ran through Arlington. Fly, Eagles, Fly.

articles.matchup: Final: Chicago Bears (9-2) 39, Detroit Lions (8-3) 35, Thu., Nov. 26, Ford Field, Detroit. Next: at Atlanta Falcons, Sun., Dec. 6, 1:00 PM ET, Mercedes-Benz Stadium, Atlanta
articles.text:
The Chicago Bears beat the Detroit Lions 39-35 at Ford Field, and the winning catch came with three seconds left on a Thanksgiving that began so well. America's Thanksgiving Parade marched down Woodward Avenue for the 100th time Thursday morning, with the Detroit Youth Choir opening it and Dan Gilbert as grand marshal. By the afternoon the party was at Ford Field, and the Bears crashed it.

Jahmyr Gibbs was the best player on the field. Twenty-one carries, 205 yards, three touchdowns. He scored from the 1 twice, then took a first-down handoff from our 30 and went 70 yards for 35-24 with 8:20 left. Amon-Ra St. Brown caught seven balls for 146 yards, and Jared Goff found Sam LaPorta for an 11-yard touchdown with six seconds left in the half to make it 19-10. We piled up 549 yards. That should be plenty.

It wasn't, and the hidden points hurt. Jake Bates pushed the extra point after the Gibbs run wide left. Rome Odunze got behind us for 41 yards a minute later, Caleb Williams ran in the two, and 35-24 was 35-32. On our next drive Goff threw for Jameson Williams at the Chicago 21 and Dillon Thieneman took it away.

Then came the decision I'll be chewing on through leftovers. With 2:22 left and a three-point lead, we went for it on fourth down at the Chicago 33 instead of trying the kick, and Goff's throw to Gibbs gained a yard. Chicago got the ball at its own 32 and needed 13 plays. A face mask on D.J. Reed gave them 15 free yards, and Odunze caught a 6-yarder in the end zone with three seconds to go. Our lateral play at the gun ended in an illegal forward flag.

Bright spots, because there were some. Malcolm Rodriguez recovered the Colston Loveland fumble at our 16 on Chicago's first drive and sacked Williams for 10 in the fourth. Roger McCreary broke up three throws. Brian Branch made two tackles for loss, and Jack Fox boomed a 61-yard punt.

This was our first home loss of the season, and it drops us to 8-3, a game behind Chicago. One hundred parades on Woodward and this city has seen worse Thursdays, so nobody in Detroit is folding. The Atlanta Falcons are next at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, Sunday, Dec. 6, at 1:00 PM ET. Grit, Detroit. Go get it back.

We gave up a safety in the last two minutes of the half, and Sam LaPorta caught an 11-yard touchdown with six seconds left for 19-10. Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 205 yards and three scores, and his 70-yard sprint with 8:20 to go made it 35-24. I tip my cap to the man. Then I stopped tipping it.

Zavion Thomas brought the kickoff back to our 29. Caleb Williams hit Luther Burden III for 15 and Odunze for 15, then dropped a 41-yard rainbow to Odunze down the right side. Williams ran the two-point try in himself. Three plays, one minute, 35-32.

Dillon Thieneman made sure Detroit didn't answer. Jared Goff threw for Jameson Williams at our 21, and Thieneman jumped it and brought it back 18 yards. We came up empty on fourth down at the Detroit 42, and Gibbs ripped off 34 more yards, but the Lions went for it on fourth down at our 33 instead of kicking, and Gibbs got one yard on the throw. Our ball at the 32 with 2:17 left.

That drive was the best football I've seen from this team in years. Williams kept it himself on fourth-and-1 at our 41. Odunze grabbed 11 more, a face mask flag on D.J. Reed handed us 15, and D'Andre Swift caught one for 12 to the Detroit 9. From the 6, Williams found Odunze in the end zone. Thirteen plays, 68 yards.

Williams finished 30 of 44 for 345 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. Swift ran for 65 and caught seven for 97, and Kyle Monangai punched in two short touchdown runs. Cam Lewis made 10 tackles, and Thieneman added seven to go with his interception.

articles.byline: Ryder Galloway, The TCU Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Texas Tech Red Raiders (11-1) 48, TCU Horned Frogs (5-7) 27, Thu., Nov. 26, Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock. Regular season complete
articles.text:
Texas Tech beat TCU 48-27 in Lubbock on Thanksgiving night, and the Horned Frogs finish 5-7, one win short of a bowl game. That morning in Fort Worth, the YMCA Turkey Trot sent runners off from General Worth Square downtown, with every dollar raised going to scholarships for local families. That was the best news a Frog fan got all day.

For one quarter, Andy Avalos had this team flying in his first game as interim coach, four days after Sonny Dykes was fired. Sam Haley recovered a muffed punt at the Tech 33, Kyle Lemmermann kicked a 33-yarder, and Adam Schobel hit Ed Small for a 3-yard touchdown with 19 seconds left in the first. Frogs 10, Red Raiders 0.

Then 75 seconds blew it all up. Thomas Castellanos found Kenny Johnson for a 19-yard touchdown at 2:08 of the second quarter. On our very next snap, Jeremy Payne lost a fumble at our 21, and Castellanos threw a 21-yard touchdown on the following play. We went three-and-out, and Malcolm Simmons returned the punt 79 yards. Schobel had already lost one on a sack at the Tech 40. It was 27-10 at the half, and Tech kept rolling until it was 41-10.

Schobel kept swinging. He went 24 of 37 for 218 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. Major Everhart ran 14 times for 138 yards, including a 49-yard burst, and we ran for 245 yards as a team. Our 18-play drive in the third quarter ate 8:59 and ended with a Lemmermann field goal. Small caught nine balls and two touchdowns, and Jacobe Hayes grabbed an 11-yard score with 1:07 left.

We held the ball for 37:31 and still lost by 21. Castellanos completed 20 of 25 for 374 yards, and our secondary never found an answer. Kylin Jackson made seven tackles and a sack, and the front fought all night.

That's the season. Five wins, a coaching change and a Thanksgiving night we'll try to forget by Saturday. The Frogs have a long winter ahead to sort out who leads this program, and I'll be back at General Worth Square next Thanksgiving morning either way. Riff Ram, Bah Bah.

articles.title: Los Angeles Rams vs Green Bay Packers Week 12: Corum's Birthday Bash, 26-13
articles.matchup: Final: Los Angeles Rams (7-4) 26, Green Bay Packers (6-5) 13, Wed., Nov. 25, SoFi Stadium, Inglewood. Next: vs Kansas City Chiefs, Thu., Dec. 3, 8:15 PM ET, SoFi Stadium, Inglewood
articles.text:
Los Angeles Rams 26, Green Bay Packers 13, and Blake Corum spent his 26th birthday running through Green Bay 32 times in the NFL's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game. We wore the Fearsome White uniforms for the first time, built to honor Deacon Jones, Merlin Olsen, Lamar Lundy and Rosey Grier. Grier, 94, was in the building, and he got a huge ovation when he was honored during a timeout.

The old Fearsome Foursome would have loved this front. Nate Landman forced a Tucker Kraft fumble on Green Bay's second drive, Quentin Lake fell on it, and Brandon McManus turned it into his second field goal. Byron Young got home on Jordan Love, and Jaylen McCollough and Emmanuel Forbes Jr. each intercepted him. Green Bay ran 14 times all night for 55 yards.

It was 13-13 at halftime, and nobody in Inglewood felt good about it. Kyren Williams had scored from 7 to finish a 79-yard drive, but Love answered with an 80-yarder of his own, and Trey Smack hit from 54 and 48. So Sean McVay handed it to Corum, and kept handing it to him.

The first drive of the second half went 14 plays and 64 yards and burned 8:02. Corum got stuffed at the 2, then at the 1, and finally plowed in from 1 yard out after a replay review for 20-13. He ran 25 times for 161 yards in the second half alone. Green Bay had the ball for 6:15 after halftime.

Matthew Stafford threw for 140 yards and didn't need a yard more. Konata Mumpfield caught four for 69. Corum ripped off 35 yards on third-and-1 to set up McManus from 40 for 23-13, then broke a 29-yarder to the Green Bay 15 on our last drive. McManus closed it from 30 with 27 seconds left. Four field goal tries, four makes, against the team he used to kick for.

One bad moment: Kamren Kinchens was ejected for the hit that knocked Christian Watson out of the game before halftime. On the bright side, McVay finally beat Matt LaFleur, his old offensive coordinator, and we snapped a five-game skid against the Packers.

Five straight wins, 7-4, and the Kansas City Chiefs come to SoFi Stadium on Thursday, Dec. 3, at 8:15 PM ET. Short turnaround, so somebody get Corum a cold tub and a slice of birthday cake. Whose house? Rams house.

articles.matchup: Final: Los Angeles Rams (7-4) 26, Green Bay Packers (6-5) 13, Wed., Nov. 25, SoFi Stadium, Inglewood. Next: at New Orleans Saints, Sun., Dec. 6, 1:00 PM ET, Caesars Superdome, New Orleans
articles.text:
The Los Angeles Rams beat the Green Bay Packers 26-13 on Thanksgiving Eve at SoFi Stadium, and Green Bay is carrying a sour taste into the holiday. Matthew Golden spent this week handing out Thanksgiving meals to families at his first Golden Turkey Giveaway. Wednesday night, the Rams ate ours.

For one half we were right there. Trey Smack drilled a 54-yarder to get us on the board, and after Kyren Williams scored from 7 for 13-3, Jordan Love went 80 yards in seven plays. Christian Watson for 21, Golden for 39 down the right side, and Watson again from 6 yards out. 13-10. Smack hit from 48 with 1:50 left in the half, and we went to the locker room tied 13-13.

That field goal drive cost us plenty. On the fourth-down throw right before it, Watson took a hit from Kamren Kinchens, who was ejected, and Watson was ruled out with a concussion. We lost our best receiver, and the night tipped right there.

Then came Blake Corum. The Rams opened the third with a 14-play, 64-yard drive that ate 8:02, and Corum finished it from the 1. 20-13. Ty'Ron Hopper gave us life with an interception of Matthew Stafford, and two plays later Love threw it right back, Jaylen McCollough grabbing it at the Rams 3. In the fourth, Love went deep for Bo Melton and Emmanuel Forbes Jr. took that one too.

Corum carried 32 times for 184 yards. The Rams ran 47 times for 241 yards and held the ball for 40:40. We had it for 19:20 and ran for 55 yards on 14 carries. You don't win in this league holding the ball for a third of the night. Brandon McManus, who used to kick for us, made all four of his field goals, the last with 27 seconds left for 26-13.

A few bright spots. Micah Parsons sacked Stafford in his season debut. Watson had four catches for 65 yards before he went down. Keisean Nixon, Evan Williams, Isaiah McDuffie and Hopper made nine tackles apiece, which tells you how often Corum came through the middle.

We're 6-5 with two straight losses. Thursday morning the Festival Foods Turkey Trot goes off at 8 a.m. outside Lambeau Field, and I'll be out there running this one off. Then a long week to heal up before we visit the Saints at Caesars Superdome, Sunday, Dec. 6, 1:00 PM ET. Get Christian Watson healthy, get the run game going. Go Pack Go.

articles.text:
Miami (OH) 28, Western Michigan 24, and true freshman Drew Bellisari had a hand in all four of our touchdowns on a 32-degree night in Kalamazoo. He threw two, ran for two, and Amariyun Knighten intercepted Broc Lowry in the end zone with 20 seconds left to finish it. We're 8-4, 6-2 in the MAC, and our title-game hopes are still alive.

In Oxford, Goggin Ice Center opens its Thanksgiving Holiday Skate on Wednesday at 3:15, eight bucks with free skate rental. I'm taking laps on that rink with my arms up. Western Michigan can keep the free tickets. We took the win.

Bellisari didn't play like a freshman for one second. He hit Maleek Huggins for 33 and Scoop Smith for a 31-yard touchdown on our first drive. Next time out he ran for 31 and found Brendan Loftus from 14. 14-3 after one quarter. Malcolm McCain intercepted Lowry at our 12 in the second, and we took the 11-point margin to the locker room.

Western Michigan came out of the half running hard. Jalen Buckley broke a 44-yarder and scored from the 3, 14-10. Bellisari answered on third-and-19, hitting Huggins for 31, then kept it himself for an 18-yard touchdown, 21-10. The Broncos scored again, and later Pierse Stainton turned a punt into a 19-yard run. That's a coaching staff that trusts its guys.

The fourth got tense. Cole Cabana broke a 41-yarder, Buckley scored from 23, and the two-point try made it 24-21 Broncos with 8:02 left. Our answer took four plays. An interference flag got us 15, D'Shawntae Jones ran for 25 on third-and-5, and Bellisari scored from 12 at 5:40. Brady Stidham's kick made it 28-24.

Then the defense had to hold up for 14 plays. Western Michigan ran for 297 yards and got to our 5. Zhaiylen Scott, who made 10 tackles, helped stuff Buckley for no gain on second down. On the next snap, Knighten caught Lowry's throw in the end zone.

Bellisari threw for 214 yards and ran for 93. Huggins caught four for 77. We had zero turnovers and took two away. Bring on Wednesday at Goggin.

articles.title: Kent State vs Eastern Michigan: Overturned at the Final Snap, 17-12
articles.byline: Ozzie Brannigan, The Kent State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Eastern Michigan Eagles (5-7) 17, Kent State Golden Flashes (3-9) 12, Tue., Nov. 24, Rynearson Stadium, Ypsilanti. Regular season complete
articles.text:
Kent State lost 17-12 at Eastern Michigan on Tuesday night, and for the length of one replay review I had both arms in the air. On the last snap, Ethan Thanthanavong found Wayne Harris in the end zone, the officials signaled touchdown, and the booth took it away. Incomplete. We finish 3-9, 2-6 in the MAC.

I'll remember Brendyn Smith before I remember that review. He caught a 17-yard touchdown throw to finish a 90-yard drive in the first quarter, and after Eastern went up 14-6, he fielded the kickoff at the goal and went 100 yards. Fourteen seconds after their score, it was 14-12. Both two-point tries failed, which is a very Kent State way to spend a good night.

Harris was the best player on the field. Five catches, 125 yards, and a 47-yarder in the third quarter that put us at the Eastern 39. We got to the 23 and came up empty on fourth down. Jakorion Caffey ground out 60 yards on 13 carries, but the rest of our ground game went nowhere, 71 rushing yards for the night.

The defense deserved a ride home with a win. Thomas Aden made eight tackles and dropped Brogan McCaughey for 14 yards to finish the third quarter. Hayden Dawahare made eight more and chased McCaughey all night. Eastern threw for 95 yards. Their 40-yard touchdown early in the fourth got wiped out by an ineligible-downfield flag, and four snaps later we stuffed them on fourth down.

Turnovers are what sank us. Bryce Llewellyn intercepted Thanthanavong at the end of the half, Hunter Hopperton had the ball punched out at the Eastern 29 in the fourth, and with 2:52 left Llewellyn intercepted another one and returned it 35 yards to our 11. Rudy Kessinger kicked a 28-yarder at 1:57. Three giveaways on somebody else's Senior Night is how you lose by five.

And still we nearly stole it. Harris beat them for 32 yards, an interference flag put us at the Eastern 15, and after a sack and a 7-yard catch by Brandon White, we had one snap from the 14. You know the rest.

Downtown Kent gets the holidays going Saturday. The City of Kent says Santa and Mrs. Claus arrive by train at 6:00 PM with Mayor Jack Amrhein on Small Business Saturday, and the countdown happens downtown, by the Main Street Bridge and the gazebo at Main and Franklin. I'll be standing by the Main Street Bridge with one request for the man in red: a replay angle that agrees with me.

articles.title: Eastern Michigan vs Kent State: Seniors Close The Factory, 17-12
articles.byline: Imogen Tremblay, The Eastern Michigan Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Eastern Michigan Eagles (5-7) 17, Kent State Golden Flashes (3-9) 12, Tue., Nov. 24, Rynearson Stadium, Ypsilanti. Regular season complete
articles.text:
Eastern Michigan 17, Kent State 12, and the 30 members of the program Eastern honored on Crosby Field before kickoff walked off it as winners. Senior Night at The Factory came with seven-dollar seats, a canned food drive for Swoop's Pantry and a 30-degree Tuesday night in Ypsilanti, and the seniors made sure nobody asked for a refund. We finish 5-7, 4-4 in the MAC, and we never trailed.

Amareon Blue needed two snaps to say hello. Benson Prosper caught a 4-yarder, then Blue went 61 yards up the middle, and it was 7-0 with 14:14 still on the first-quarter clock. Blue finished with 137 yards on 20 carries, and he ran like a guy who was tired of hearing about the cold.

Kent State answered with a 90-yard drive and a 17-yard touchdown throw to Brendyn Smith, 7-6. Decorie Johnson punched in a 7-yard run late in the second quarter for 14-6, and then Smith took the kickoff 100 yards right back at us. Fourteen seconds of game clock. I'm still mad about it. The good news: both Kent State two-point tries failed, and senior captain Bryce Llewellyn intercepted Ethan Thanthanavong at our 27 to close the half at 14-12.

The third quarter was a punting contest, and Daniel Hull won it. He dropped six of his seven punts inside the 20. Then the fourth quarter tried to break my heart. Brogan McCaughey hit Harold Mack for 40 yards and a touchdown, and an ineligible-downfield flag wiped it out. Fine. Zach Mowchan, another senior captain, punched the ball loose from Hunter Hopperton at our 29, and Quincy Byas fell on it.

With 2:52 to go, Llewellyn jumped Thanthanavong again and ran it back 35 yards to the Kent State 11. Rudy Kessinger, who missed from 52 earlier, knocked through a 28-yarder at 1:57 with senior Jack Kautz snapping it. 17-12.

Kent State made us sweat to the last tick. Wayne Harris, who caught five balls for 125 yards, got loose for 32, an interference flag put them at our 15, and senior Ronn Hardin buried Thanthanavong for a 7-yard sack. On the final snap, Thanthanavong threw to Harris in the end zone, the officials signaled touchdown, and the replay review turned it into an incompletion. Llewellyn got a hand on that ball. Nine tackles, two interceptions and the last breakup of the night, all on his Senior Night.

Our defense held Kent State to 71 rushing yards and took the ball away three times without giving it back once. Thirty seniors, one last Tuesday at The Factory, and not one snap spent behind. Bring the cans next November, Ypsilanti. We'll bring the defense.
